author: vmadananth
title: GPU unit tests fail with a burst of 37 gtest-parallel worker crashes right after fp16_scale_out accuracy mismatch
signature: GPU unit tests accuracy tolerance mismatch in fusion test (val_ref vs val_opt difference exceeds tolerance in fusion_test_common.hpp) followed by burst of concurrent gtest-parallel worker processes exiting with code 3|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 accuracy mismatch (diff 3.05e-05 > tolerance 1e-05), immediately followed by 36 more tests (mostly convolution_random_smoke_test and fusings_gpu cases) exiting with code 3

key_errors:
fusion_test_common.hpp(90): error: The difference between val_ref[i] and val_opt[i] is 3.0517578125e-05, which exceeds tolerance, where
val_ref[i] evaluates to -0.04473876953125,
val_opt[i] evaluates to -0.044769287109375, and
tolerance evaluates to 9.9999997473787516e-06.
[  FAILED  ] fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1
root_cause: The first test (fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1) fails on a borderline floating-point accuracy mismatch (3.05e-05 vs a 1e-05 tolerance) comparing fused vs. non-fused GPU kernel outputs - a known tight-tolerance flake on this Windows iGPU runner. Immediately afterward, 36 more gtest-parallel worker processes (convolution and fusion tests) exit silently with code 3, matching the previously-tracked runner-resource-exhaustion signature. The merged PR (#39011, 'Gpu fc weights layout') is documented as an infrastructure-only change (new weights_layout attribute, no behavior change) and does not touch pooling/fusion kernels or accuracy-sensitive code paths referenced in the failing tests, so this is consistent with the pre-existing recurring iGPU runner flake rather than a regression introduced by this commit. This is the 7th recorded occurrence of signature 502c01bffd8f35db.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside the CI Windows iGPU runner. Locally: build ov_gpu_unit_tests, run with gtest_parallel.py at similar worker concurrency against an Intel iGPU device, and repeat fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 and nearby convolution_random_smoke_test cases many times under concurrent load.
recommended_actions: Investigate reducing gtest-parallel worker concurrency for GPU unit tests on Windows iGPU runners to avoid resource exhaustion under concurrent kernel execution.
Review/relax the fusion accuracy tolerance in fusion_test_common.hpp for fp16_scale_out-style comparisons, or adjust the reference computation to reduce the fp16/fp32 rounding gap.

Escalate to the iGPU CI runner pool owners: this is the 7th occurrence of the same signature in a short time window; consider temporarily marking affected convolution/fusion tests as known-flaky or capping test parallelism until root-caused.
Add retry-on-failure for the worker-crash burst specifically in gtest-parallel GPU test runs to avoid repeatedly blocking post-commit merges on this transient runner issue.
prevention_strategies: Add CI-level detection that treats a cluster of worker exit-code-3 failures immediately following an accuracy-tolerance failure as a known runner-resource-exhaustion signature, auto-retrying the GPU unit test job once before failing the pipeline. Track GPU resource utilization/memory pressure metrics during gtest-parallel runs to correlate with worker concurrency.
historical_context: This exact signature (502c01bffd8f35db) has recurred 6 times previously across unrelated commits (runs 43369335165, 43398624960, 43430895182, 43440149471, 43461440649, 43473585791), always starting with the same fp16_scale_out accuracy mismatch followed by a burst of worker crashes. This run is the 7th occurrence, further confirming it is a persistent runner/infrastructure-level flake unrelated to the merged PR's content.
